chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'We invited a man to the entirety of what we are upon, from the entirety of Islam, so he accepted it. Then he drank wine, committed adultery, and consumed usury, and nothing from the permissible and the prohibited had been explained to him. Would the penalty be established upon him if he was ignorant of it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if proof is established upon him that he had previously accepted with its prohibition.'
ai.seo_question: Does ignorance of prohibition exempt a person from the Hadd penalty in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that mere commission of major sins like drinking wine or adultery does not automatically incur the Hadd penalty if the perpetrator was ignorant of their prohibition. The Imam specifies that legal accountability requires proof that the individual had previously acknowledged the specific prohibition, thereby distinguishing between general ignorance and persistent defiance. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that knowledge of the ruling is a prerequisite for the full application of corporal punishments.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘We invited a man to the entirety of what we are upon, from the entirety of Al-Islam, so he accepted with it, then he drank the wine, and commited adultery, and consumed the usury, and nothing from the Permissibles and the Prohibtions had been explained to him. Would the Penalty (Hadd) be established upon him, when he was ignorant of it?’ Heasws said: ‘No, except if the proof were to be established upon him that he had previously accepted with these prohibitions’.
